story.title: Alice in Wonderland
story.description: Chasing after a hurried rabbit, a young girl falls into a world where nothing follows the rules she knows.
story.author: Lewis Carroll

chapters.name: Nothing Is What It Seems
chapters.summary: Alice follows something impossible out of boredom and lands somewhere with rules of its own, none of which anybody will explain.

chapters.name: Rules Without Reason
chapters.summary: Wonderland is not lawless. Its laws are perfectly consistent and completely arbitrary, and Alice is the only person present who finds that worth objecting to.

chapters.name: The Queen's Court
chapters.summary: The Queen sentences first and tries afterwards. Alice can leave the court quietly or say out loud that the whole thing is nonsense, and the two roads end differently.

scenes.name: The rabbit hole
scenes.summary: A white rabbit in a waistcoat takes a watch out of its pocket and says it is late. Alice follows it across a field and down a hole without once considering how she will get back up.

scenes.name: The hall of little doors
scenes.summary: She lands in a long hall of locked doors, and behind a curtain finds one fifteen inches high onto the loveliest garden she has ever seen. The key is on a glass table she cannot reach without being smaller, and the door is too small to pass through while she can reach the key.

scenes.name: Drink me, eat me
scenes.summary: A bottle marked DRINK ME shrinks her past the key; a cake marked EAT ME sends her to the ceiling. She cries a pool of tears at nine feet tall and nearly drowns in it at three inches.

scenes.name: The grinning cat
scenes.summary: The Cheshire Cat appears in a tree by the tail first, and answers every question Alice asks with something true and useless. It tells her that everyone here is mad, including her, and offers to prove it by directions.

scenes.name: The mad tea party
scenes.summary: The Hatter and the March Hare are stuck at six o'clock because the Hatter quarrelled with Time, and Time has refused to move for him since. They ask Alice a riddle with no answer and are offended when she asks for one.

scenes.name: Painting the roses red
scenes.summary: Three playing cards are painting a white rose bush red before the Queen sees it. They planted the wrong tree, and the punishment for the mistake is worse than the punishment for the fraud, so they are committing the fraud.

scenes.name: The croquet game
scenes.summary: The Queen plays croquet with live flamingos for mallets and hedgehogs for balls, on a ground that will not hold still. Nobody keeps score, because everyone is too busy being sentenced to bother finishing a turn.

scenes.name: A quiet dismissal
scenes.summary: Alice disagrees with the Queen carefully, in the mildest words she can find. The Queen is annoyed, has nothing specific to charge her with, and lets the matter drop in front of the whole court.

scenes.name: Off with her head
scenes.summary: Alice says plainly that the Queen is nothing but a playing card. The Queen screams for her execution, and the court is far more shocked by the observation than by the sentence.

scenes.name: The trial of the Knave
scenes.summary: The Knave of Hearts is tried for stealing tarts, with the verdict already written. Alice, growing larger by the minute, points out that the evidence proves nothing, and the King rules that she is out of order.

scenes.name: Waking on the bank
scenes.summary: Alice is on the riverbank with her head in her sister's lap and leaves falling on her face. She tells the whole thing as a dream, and cannot decide, in the telling, whether that makes it smaller.

scenes.name: Staying for the sentence
scenes.summary: Alice refuses to be dismissed and calls the court what it is: a pack of cards. They rise into the air and come down on her, and she meets them full height, awake, and unafraid.

characters.name: Alice
characters.description: A curious girl who prefers a strange adventure to an ordinary afternoon. She is the only person in Wonderland who keeps expecting things to make sense, and the only one anything is ever explained to.
characters.personality: Endlessly curious and quick to speak her mind, rarely frightened for long by what she sees.
characters.motivation: Wants to make sense of Wonderland's strange rules and find her way back above ground.
characters.qualities: Polite, logical, and remarkably composed in the face of nonsense.
characters.weaknesses: Too curious for her own good, and easily swept along into trouble.
characters.biography: A well-mannered girl who, bored on a riverbank, follows a talking rabbit down a hole and spends an afternoon lost in a world where nothing behaves as it should.
characters.plannedTimeline: Wakes up on the riverbank at the story's end, leaving Wonderland behind as an extraordinary dream.

characters.name: The White Rabbit
characters.description: Always late, always checking his pocket watch, and terrified of the Queen. He is the first impossible thing Alice sees and the reason she is here at all.
characters.personality: Perpetually anxious and fussy, obsessed with punctuality.
characters.motivation: Desperate not to be late for the Duchess and dreading the Queen's temper.
characters.weaknesses: So absorbed in his own worries that he barely notices Alice at all.
characters.biography: A White Rabbit who dashes past Alice muttering about being late, and whose disappearance down a hole is what draws her into Wonderland in the first place.
characters.plannedTimeline: Reappears throughout Wonderland, always in a hurry, never stopping long enough to explain anything.

characters.name: The Mad Hatter
characters.description: Host of a tea party that never ends, having once been sentenced by the Queen for murdering time. Since then Time has stopped moving for him, which he treats as a scheduling problem.
characters.personality: Whimsical and quick to argue about time, fond of riddles with no real answers.
characters.motivation: Keeps the tea party going, seemingly stuck at six o'clock forever.
characters.weaknesses: Cannot seem to escape his own tea party, or make much sense to outsiders.
characters.biography: Host of a tea party frozen in time ever since he quarreled with Time itself.
characters.plannedTimeline: Remains at the table, endlessly shuffling seats with the March Hare and the Dormouse.

characters.name: The Cheshire Cat
characters.description: A cat that appears and vanishes at will, in any order it likes, always grinning. It is the only creature in Wonderland that tells Alice the truth, and it is never once useful.
characters.personality: Calm and sly, amused by everyone's confusion - including the confusion his own riddles cause.
characters.motivation: Enjoys unsettling visitors with his ability to appear and vanish at will.
characters.qualities: Wise in his own strange way, unbothered by anything.
characters.weaknesses: Gives advice that is almost never straightforward enough to actually help.
characters.biography: A grinning cat who can fade in and out of sight, sometimes leaving only his smile behind.
characters.plannedTimeline: Points Alice toward the Queen's court before fading out of the story.

characters.name: The Queen of Hearts
characters.title: Ruler of the card kingdom
characters.description: A ruler with an explosive temper who orders an execution roughly once a scene. None of them are ever carried out, which nobody tells Alice.
characters.personality: Tyrannical and quick to anger, prone to shouting "Off with their head!" at the smallest offense.
characters.motivation: Demands absolute obedience and control over her court of playing cards.
characters.qualities: A commanding presence, never openly questioned by her subjects.
characters.weaknesses: Her threats are all bark - executions are ordered constantly but never actually carried out.
characters.biography: The volatile ruler of Wonderland's card kingdom, who hosts a chaotic croquet match and rules her court through fear alone.
characters.plannedTimeline: Ultimately dismisses Alice from her court, the moment that ends Alice's dream.

characters.name: The Knave of Hearts
characters.description: Accused of stealing the Queen's tarts and tried on evidence that says nothing at all. He never speaks in his own defence, having grasped earlier than Alice how the court works.

locations.name: Wonderland
locations.description: The world on the far side of the rabbit hole. Its rules are perfectly consistent with one another and with nothing else, which is what makes them so difficult to argue against.
locations.climate: Ever-changing, from garden warmth to sudden weather with no clear pattern.
locations.culture: A patchwork of nonsensical customs where playing cards, animals, and objects all speak and hold court like people.
locations.politics: Nominally ruled by the Queen of Hearts, whose word is law even when it makes no sense.

locations.name: The Queen of Hearts' Castle
locations.description: A castle of painted roses and playing-card servants, where the Queen's word is law for exactly as long as she is in the room and the King quietly reverses it after she leaves.
locations.climate: Always outdoors, at a long table permanently set for tea.
locations.culture: An endless tea party where seats are shuffled constantly and riddles pass for conversation.
locations.politics: No rule beyond the Hatter's own whims - and his ongoing feud with Time.

locations.name: The Croquet Ground
locations.description: The Queen's lawn, played with live flamingos and hedgehogs on ground that moves. Losing politely is as dangerous here as winning, and nobody has ever finished a game.
locations.climate: A tidy garden framed by rose bushes, some famously painted red to hide a mistake.
locations.culture: A rigid card-kingdom court built around croquet games and royal processions.
locations.politics: Absolute monarchy - the Queen's temper decides who is in favor and who is sentenced, if only in name.

locations.name: The Duchess's Wood
locations.description: The wood between the castle and the tea table, where the Cheshire Cat appears in pieces and gives directions that are entirely accurate and no help whatsoever.

locations.name: The Mad Hatter's House
locations.description: Where a tea party goes on without end, always at six o'clock, because the Hatter quarrelled with Time and Time has not moved for him since.

worldRules.title: The Logic of Wonderland
worldRules.description: Wonderland is not lawless. Every rule in it is applied with complete consistency and rests on nothing at all, which is why arguing against one always sounds like the objection of somebody who has missed the point.

worldRules.title: Eat Me, Drink Me
worldRules.description: Wonderland is full of food and drink bearing instructions, and the instructions are always honest about what they do and silent about how much. Size here is a thing that happens to Alice rather than a thing she has.

worldRules.title: Nobody Is Ever Actually Executed
worldRules.description: The Queen orders a beheading roughly once a scene, and the King quietly pardons every one of them behind her back. The threat is real to Alice and to nobody else, which is what makes the court unbearable rather than dangerous.

notes.title: Continuity: what size is she
notes.body: Alice changes height eight times and it matters in every scene where it happens. Track it explicitly - the trial only works because she is growing while it runs.

notes.title: Visual motif: instructions on things
notes.body: Labels, signs, verdicts written before trials. Wonderland keeps telling Alice what to do in writing, and the writing is never wrong and never sufficient.

notes.title: Revision goal: the branch is a temperament
notes.body: The two endings turn on one thing: whether Alice says the quiet thing or the loud one. Every choice on the way there should be recognisably the same decision, made smaller.

items.name: Bottle labeled "DRINK ME"
items.description: A small bottle on a glass table with a paper label, tasting of cherry tart, custard, pineapple, roast turkey, toffee and hot buttered toast at once. It makes whoever drinks it smaller.

items.name: Cake labeled "EAT ME"
items.description: A very small cake under the glass table with EAT ME marked out on it in currants. It does the opposite of the bottle, and just as suddenly.

items.name: The White Rabbit's Pocket Watch
items.description: The watch the White Rabbit keeps taking out of his waistcoat. It always tells him he is late, and it is the first impossible thing Alice decides is worth following.
